newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldier kills, wounds Arabs in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier kills, wounds Arabs in Hebron.

text.p: An Israeli soldier opened fire in all directions in the West Bank town of Hebron, killing a Palestinian and wounding others in the Arab market on Wednesday, witnesses said.
"One was killed and 10 were wounded," said Jibril Rajoub, chief of Palestinian security in the West Bank.
It was not immediately clear why the gunman opened fire. Witnesses said the man emptied an entire magazine of his M-16 before soldiers arrested him and seized the gun.
The incident occurred just as Israel and the Palestinians neared a deal for Israel to hand over most of the West Bank town to Palestinian self-rule.
Security sources identified the gunman as a Jewish settler from Maale Adumim near Jerusalem.

Witnesses said he was a young man who wore an army uniform and on his head the skullcap of a religious Jew. The army said the soldier was not posted to Hebron, but went on his own to the town, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.

"I was sitting in the market and all of a sudden there was automatic firing. I fell on the ground, but the shooting continued. I was shot in the leg," Abdul-Karim al-Atrash, a vegetable vendor, told Voice of Palestine radio.
He said there was no stone-throwing by Palestinians which might have triggered the shooting.
Israeli Major-General Gabi Ofir, in charge of the West Bank, said troops were trying to restore calm in the town. Palestinian police were asked to help.

"This incident is very serious, simply very serious," Ofir told army radio. "A soldier dressed in uniform with a long M-16 opened fire at Arab residents in Gross Square which is next to the Jewish enclave of Avraham Avinu."
Israeli Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told army radio he did not expect the incident to affect plans by Israel and the PLO to press ahead with a deal on Hebron.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said earlier on Wednesday he and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had yet to fix a summit to sew up a deal giving self-rule to Hebron.
There was no immediate reaction to the shooting from Netanyahu's office.
Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town, home to 100,000 Arabs.

Three years ago a Jew from nearby Kiryat Arba settlement, dressed in an Israeli army uniform, massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in the tomb of the biblical patriarchs before survivors beat him to death.

Israel and the Palestinians greeted the new year much the way they had spent the old one -- haggling over promised withdrawals and elusive peace deals. The handover of most of Hebron to the Palestinians has been delayed for nine months by Israeli security concerns.

Jewish settlers in the town had said they were praying for a miracle to prevent Israeli troops from pulling back and warned of impending bloodshed. They scuffled with Palestinians on Tuesday and tried to take over Arab houses in the casbah.
"I appeal even at this moment to the prime minister: Don't sign an agreement that will endanger our lives," Hebron settler leader Rabbi Moshe Levinger told Israel Radio on Wednesday.

But chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told army radio after the shooting: "We have always been arguing with the Israeli government, and the previous government actually, that the real threat to peace is not the Palestinians.
"It's these settlers, these Israeli settlers," he said.
Jewish settlers, who number 130,000 in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, helped Netanyahu sweep to power in elections last May on a promise to be tough with the Palestinians.
But Netanyahu has come under pressure from Washington, Israel's closest ally, to honour peace deals and withdraw from Hebron, the last of seven West Bank towns due for self-rule.
